subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should that live as shared execution policy rather than a Telegram-only boolean?
rationale: Source inspection proves the requested mode is absent, but deciding when an operator identity may skip approval prompts changes a security boundary and config contract that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

options.title: Keep the current approval model
options.body: Decline the bypass and document that operators who want no prompts must use existing exec/elevated full policy with permissive host approvals.

options.title: Add Telegram-only shortcut
options.body: Implement the proposed Telegram config directly, accepting a narrower patch but higher risk of policy drift from shared approvals and elevated execution.

recommendation.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is product/security policy and config-surface direction before Telegram or approval-path implementation ownership matters.
